summary: The PR adds an optional `limit` argument to `Table.search()` that slices results to at most `limit` documents, preserving storage order. `limit=None` (default) leaves behavior unchanged. It works on named tables since `Table.search` is shared. All 234 tests pass, including the 3 new limit tests.

checks.claim: search(cond, limit=N) returns at most N matches in storage order
checks.evidence: snippet: limit=1 returned [0], limit=2 returned [0,1], limit=100 returned all 5; tests/test_limit_seed.py passes

checks.claim: limit=None returns all results, unchanged behavior

checks.evidence: snippet: t.search(..., limit=2) returned 2; test_limit_on_named_table passes

findings.text: Negative limit values (e.g. limit=-1) return all results due to Python list slicing semantics; this is harmless but undocumented.
